title: Preflight checks that pass when they should not: the block-age check accepts an Infinity tolerance and any block dated in the future, the honeypot-checker check accepts any contract code at the address, and the cross-env rules read ENABLED_CHAINS with a different default from the registry

evidence.note: blockAgeSec <= tolerance: a negative age (block timestamp ahead of local time, or a wrong local clock) always passes
passed = code !== '0x': any contract at the configured address passes, not the HoneypotChecker bytecode
ENABLED_CHAINS || '' (no chain) versus chainRegistry.ts:644 || 'eth': with ENABLED_CHAINS unset, rules 1, 2 and 4 check nothing while eth is enabled
passthrough chains (Base, Arbitrum) always pass MEV health (no private path by design)
codex (22-27 independent second opinion, graded S2): Infinity passes configuration checks and disables RPC freshness protection

sibling_sites_checked: All nine preflight checks read: wallet balance and entry affordability fail closed on RPC error (:220-233, :462-477); chainId compares exactly; the anti-rug 7-day gate is time-based (SC-11, ANTIRUG slice); stale-data never blocks by design. With ENABLED_CHAINS unset the registry itself still exits on a missing FLASHBOTS_AUTH_KEY (chainRegistry.ts:948-951), so rule 1 is covered there.
severity_rationale: S3: each gap needs an operator mistake (Infinity tolerance, wrong address) or a clock problem and is backed by another layer (the registry FATALs, the honeypot dispatch returns unknown on a non-checker contract); misleading rather than capital-affecting at the base SHA.
recommendation: Require a finite tolerance with an upper bound, treat a future block beyond a small skew as a failure, compare the checker code hash with the deployed artifact, and parse ENABLED_CHAINS in one place. Card DB-04 (preflight strictness). Phase 29.
